question.problem: If $f(x,y,z)=x{e}^{2y-z},$ use the differential $\text{d}f$ to estimate the change $Δf$ in the value of $f(x,y,z)$ from $(-1,2,3)$ to $(1,0,1).$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find the differential:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(x,y,z) & =(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}x+(\frac{∂f}{∂y})\,\text{d}y+(\frac{∂f}{∂x})\,\text{d}z \\  & ={e}^{2y-z}\,\text{d}x+2x{e}^{2y-z}\,\text{d}y-x{e}^{2y-z}\,\text{d}z\end{aligned}
$$

At the point $(-1,2,3),$ the differential is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{d}f(-1,2,3) & ={e}^{2(2)-3}\,\text{d}x+2\cdot (-1)\cdot {e}^{2(2)-3}\,\text{d}y-(-1)\cdot {e}^{2(2)-3}\,\text{d}z \\  & =e\,\text{d}x-2e\,\text{d}y+e\,\text{d}z.\end{aligned}
$$

So, if we move to the point $(-1+Δx,2+Δy,3+Δz),$ then we can approximate the change in $f$ as

$$
Δf≈e\,Δx-2e\,Δy+e\,Δz.
$$

Moving from $(-1,2,3)$ to $(1,0,1),$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δx & =1-(-1)=2, \\ Δy & =0-2=-2 \\ Δz & =1-3=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Δf & ≈e\,Δx-2e\,Δy+e\,Δz \\  & ≈e\cdot (2)-2e\cdot (-2)+e\cdot (-2) \\  & ≈4e.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the value of $f(x,y,z)$ increases by approximately $4e.$
